Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

threaten verb

be about to happen: of danger, of a storm

also loom, be imminent, hang over, impending, it looks like rain

classical

Cic. Rosc. Am. 31: licet undique omnēs in mē terrōrēs impendeant (Lewis & Short)
Plaut. Ep. 1.1.77

impendeō, impendēre

verb, second conjugation, intransitive: with the dative or in + accusative

hang over, threaten, be imminent

Properly, to hang over (a rock, a sword: Cic. Tusc. 5.62); of dangers and troubles, to threaten.

Other words

  • immineō, imminēre — loom over; be close at hand

    verb, second conjugation, intransitive, with the dative · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.91: mors … cotīdiē imminet (Lewis & Short); Suet. Tit. 9: perīculum ambōbus

    Properly, to overhang or rise above (a hill over a town, Verg. A. 1.420); then of what is near and threatening: death, danger, war. Of a person, it also means to be eager for something (Cic. Phil. 5.20).

  • minor, minārī, minātus sum — threaten (of things)

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Planc. 95: dēflagrātiōnem urbī minābātur (Lewis & Short)

    Of things as well as people: a house on fire “threatened the city with burning” (Cic. Planc. 95).

Examples

  • tantae in tē impendent ruīnae

    such ruin hangs over youPlaut. Ep. 1.1.77 (Lewis & Short)

  • Nūbēs impendent; properēmus domum.

    The clouds look threatening; let’s hurry home.composed

See also threaten, threat, risk.

SourcesLewis & Short: impendeo · Lewis & Short: immineo · Lewis & Short: minor
